The per-user/customer/mixed preference fallback chain is a layered-config resolution problem — define a strict precedence order and a deterministic tie-break, and fail loud on an unresolvable 'mixed' spec rather than defaulting silently to one system.

pass1.buildNote: Checkpoint writes must survive disk-full (write-temp-then-rename, check ENOSPC) and use a monotonic clock so clock-skew can't corrupt recovery ordering.

pass2.systemImpact: CADCrashRecoveryPlatformEngine is the platform-hardening layer beneath CADCrashRecoveryEngine (U-CAD-APP-13) — it handles orphan COM processes, disk-full checkpoints, and clock-skew. Every long CAD automation job on the memory-pressured PRISM host depends on it; if a disk-full checkpoint corrupts instead of failing loud, recovery replays from a truncated checkpoint and produces a wrong model.
csDepth: Disk-full-safe checkpointing means write-temp-then-rename AND explicitly checking for ENOSPC on both write and fsync — a rename onto a full disk can still fail; the engine must surface ENOSPC loud, never leave a partial checkpoint as the 'latest'.

Clock-skew resilience requires a monotonic clock for ordering recovery events — wall-clock timestamps can go backwards (NTP correction), making a later checkpoint appear older; orphan-COM detection by 'process older than N seconds' must also use monotonic time or a backwards jump reaps a live process.

csKnowledge: experience replay buffer with prioritized sampling
pass1.buildNote: EWC++ needs the Fisher information matrix computed over prior tasks — test against a real continual-learning sequence that would forget without the penalty.

pass2.systemImpact: ContinualLearningBufferEngine (EWC++ + replay buffer) is the catastrophic-forgetting guard for every PRISM learning engine that updates online — CADCAM-AGI's VariabilityIntegrationLayer (U-AGI18) and the CAD learning engines (U-CTE12 targets) depend on it so that adapting to a new customer's parts doesn't erase prior-customer competence. csDepth: The Fisher information matrix is O(params²) if stored densely — use the diagonal approximation (standard EWC) and persist only the diagonal, but document that the approximation drops parameter correlations; full Fisher is intractable for any non-trivial model.

Prioritized replay sampling needs a sum-tree (segment tree) for O(log n) proportional sampling and priority update — a naive linear scan over the buffer is O(n) per sample and dominates training time; importance-sampling weights must correct the bias the prioritization introduces.

CAD-GROUND-TRUTH-MS0::U-CGT06.title: CADScreenshotCapturer — reference views for visual diff

csKnowledge: deterministic camera/view orientation for repeatable capture
pass1.buildNote: Reference-view capture must be deterministic (fixed camera, lighting, resolution) or visual diff produces false regressions.

pass2.systemImpact: CADScreenshotCapturer produces the reference views that CADVisualDiffEngine and the CAD regression dashboard (U-CINF09) compare against — every visual-diff regression verdict depends on these captures being byte-deterministic. Non-deterministic capture (varying camera, lighting, AA) generates false visual regressions that erode trust in the whole regression suite.

Perceptual image hashing (pHash/dHash) has a false-negative rate — a real but small geometric change can hash within tolerance; the diff threshold is a precision/recall tradeoff that must be tuned against a labeled set, not guessed.

pass1.buildNote: 20K-file parallel extraction needs bounded worker pool + checkpointing — a crash at file 12K must resume, not restart.

pass2.systemImpact: GroundTruthBatchExtractor produces the entire 20K-file ground-truth corpus — it is the single upstream dependency of GroundTruthRegistryEngine (U-CGT08), the CAD ML training units (U-ML-11), and CAD-INFRA-MS0's regression corpus. A crash that restarts from zero instead of resuming wastes hours; a checkpoint bug that skips files silently shrinks the corpus and biases every model trained on it.
csDepth: Bounded-concurrency worker pool: the worker count must be tuned to the memory-pressured PRISM host (commit-memory ceiling), not CPU count — over-subscription triggers the fleet-memory-monitor critical state and OOM; a semaphore-bounded pool with backpressure is the correct structure.

Resumable checkpointing must record per-file completion atomically (an append-only .jsonl of completed file ids) — a checkpoint that records a count rather than the set of done files cannot distinguish 'file 12001-12100 done' from 'a different 100 done', causing skip-or-redo on resume.

pass1.buildNote: Registry must be queryable by class and feature — build an index, not a linear scan; persist it with an atomic write + schemaVersion.

pass2.systemImpact: GroundTruthRegistryEngine is the queryable index over the ground-truth corpus from U-CGT07 — CAD ML training (U-ML-11), regression validation (U-CINF14), and any consistency-validation unit query it by class/feature. If the index is stale or its persisted form is corrupt, every consumer silently trains/validates against a partial corpus.
csDepth: An inverted index keyed by class/feature must be built once and updated incrementally — a linear scan over 20K records per query is O(n) and unusable; the index posting lists should be sorted for fast intersection on multi-term queries.

Persisting the index atomically with schemaVersion is mandatory — a reader hitting a mid-write index file sees truncated JSON; if the index grows large, prefer an append-only or sharded store over rewriting one big JSON, since pretty-printing a multi-hundred-MB structure hits V8's max-string-length cap.

pass1.buildNote: Determinism test must fail when output drifts — assert byte-identical results across runs against a real ground-truth corpus, not a stub.

pass2.systemImpact: The ground-truth determinism regression test is the fail-on-revert oracle that protects the entire CAD-GROUND-TRUTH-MS0 corpus — it guards U-CGT01/02/03/07/08 against silent extraction drift. If this test passes when output drifts, every downstream ML and regression milestone trains against a moving target without knowing it.

A real fail-on-revert oracle must actually fail on the buggy code — write it so that reverting the determinism fix flips the test red; a test that passes against both correct and buggy output is a worthless toBeDefined-class stub.

pass1.buildNote: 20K-file catalog must be incrementally updatable (mtime-keyed) and persisted atomically — a full rewalk on every change won't scale.

pass2.systemImpact: CADFileIndexerEngine is the master 20,006-file catalog that CADFileClassifierEngine (U-CINF02), the CAD universal-control coverage telemetry (U-CUC16), and the new-customer-directory watcher (U-CUC05) all read. If the incremental mtime-keyed update misses a changed file, the entire CAD coverage picture and every downstream classifier silently operates on a stale catalog.
csDepth: mtime-keyed incremental indexing has a known false-negative: a file modified within the same second as the last index pass, or restored with a preserved mtime, is missed — pair mtime with size and optionally a content hash for changed-file detection; bounded-depth recursion prevents runaway on symlink loops.

Persisting a 20K-entry catalog atomically means temp+rename, and at this scale prefer not pretty-printing the JSON (compact stringify) — the system-viz fs-coverage work documents the V8 max-string-length crash from indented stringify of large merged graphs.

pass1.buildNote: Classify by file signature + extension, not extension alone — assert every class branch in tests with real example files.

pass2.systemImpact: CADFileClassifierEngine labels every cataloged file part/assembly/drawing/CAM — CAD-INFRA-MS0's regression infra (U-CINF14 smoke corpus) and coverage telemetry (U-CUC16) partition work by these classes. A misclassification routes a file to the wrong test/extraction lane, so a drawing tested as a part silently produces a false regression or a skipped check.

An 'unknown/other' bucket must be surfaced loudly, not silently swallowed — an unclassified file is a coverage gap; a rule classifier should emit a confidence and route low-confidence cases to a human-review queue.

pass1.buildNote: Per-file state must carry schemaVersion and write atomically — a reader hitting a mid-write file must never see truncated JSON.

pass2.systemImpact: CADTestStateSchema defines the per-file atomic state record that CADTestCheckpointEngine (U-CINF05), CADFailureTriageEngine (U-CINF06), and CADRegressionResultsAnalyzerEngine (U-CINF10) all read and write — it is the shared data contract for the whole CAD regression pipeline. A schema change without a migration path breaks every consumer at once.
csDepth: Per-file atomic state means each file's state record is its own temp+rename write — this avoids the multi-writer race entirely (no shared mutable JSON), and a reader hitting a mid-write file must never see truncated JSON; the rename is the atomicity guarantee.

Every state JSON requires schemaVersion and an N-1 backward-compatible migration — a Zod schema validates on read, but the analyzer must read schemaVersion FIRST and dispatch to the right field mapping; assuming current field names against an older record is the recurring schema-read-blindness bug class.

csKnowledge: checkpoint / resume pattern every N units
pass1.buildNote: Checkpoint every 100 files atomically — restart must resume from the last good checkpoint without re-processing or skipping files.

pass2.systemImpact: CADTestCheckpointEngine makes the CAD regression run resumable every 100 files — the 20K-file regression sweep (and U-CINF14's smoke validation) depends on it so a crash at file 12K resumes rather than restarts. A checkpoint bug that skips or re-runs files corrupts CADRegressionResultsAnalyzerEngine's (U-CINF10) aggregate pass-rate.
csDepth: The checkpoint must record the SET of completed file ids (append-only), not a count — restart logic that resumes 'after file N' assumes processing order is stable; if order varies (parallel workers), only an explicit done-set lets resume skip exactly the done files.

Atomic checkpoint write (temp+rename) every 100 files is a throughput/durability tradeoff — too-frequent checkpointing serializes the workers on fsync; the 100-file interval bounds re-work to at most 100 files on a crash, which is the right granularity.

pass1.buildNote: Every failure must land in a named category — an unclassified failure is a finding; never let one fall through to an 'unknown' silent bucket.

pass2.systemImpact: CADFailureTriageEngine classifies every CAD regression failure into a named category — CADRegressionResultsAnalyzerEngine (U-CINF10), the dashboard (U-CINF09), and the safety hooks (U-CINF13) all consume its taxonomy to decide aggregate health and whether to abort. An uncategorized failure falling into a silent 'unknown' bucket hides a whole class of breakage from the abort gate.
csDepth: Exception-type-to-category mapping must have a total function semantics — every failure lands in a named category, and a genuinely new exception type must surface as a LOUD 'needs-a-rule' finding, not default into an 'unknown' sink that the analyzer then under-weights.

Rule-based triage ordering matters: a broad rule placed before a specific one shadows it (the same first-match-wins shadowing hazard as ABAC policy ordering); order rules specific-to-general and test the overlap cases.

pass1.buildNote: Store diffs/images/logs content-addressed so identical artifacts dedupe — write blobs atomically and key by hash.

pass2.systemImpact: CADArtifactStorageEngine content-addresses the diffs/images/logs produced by the CAD regression run — CADRegressionDashboardUI (U-CINF09) and CADRegressionReportGeneratorEngine (U-CINF11) link to its blobs. If two identical artifacts don't dedupe, storage bloats; if a blob write is non-atomic, the dashboard links to a truncated image.
csDepth: Content-addressable storage keyed by SHA-256 gives free deduplication but a hash collision (astronomically unlikely with SHA-256, but a malformed-input bug can compute the wrong hash) writes one blob over another — verify hash on read for safety-relevant artifacts.

Atomic blob write (temp+rename into the hash-named final path) makes the store idempotent: re-storing an identical artifact is a no-op; this also makes concurrent writers safe since both produce the same final name and the rename is atomic.

csKnowledge: web dashboard rendering from JSON state
pass1.buildNote: Dashboard renders from the regression results JSON — verify the UI reflects real aggregated metrics, not hardcoded placeholder data.

pass2.systemImpact: CADRegressionDashboardUI is the operator-facing surface for the whole CAD regression infra — it renders CADRegressionResultsAnalyzerEngine's (U-CINF10) aggregate metrics and CADArtifactStorageEngine's (U-CINF07) artifacts. If it renders hardcoded placeholder data, operators trust a green dashboard while real regressions go unnoticed.
csDepth: The dashboard must render purely from the regression results JSON — no derived metrics computed in the UI layer, or the dashboard and the analyzer disagree (two surfaces, one metric, two answers); the analyzer is the single source of truth.

React state management for a large result set needs virtualization/pagination — rendering 20K result rows in one DOM tree is a performance cliff; the API endpoint should serve paginated/aggregated slices, not the raw set.

csDepth: PDF/HTML generation from structured data must round-trip-verify the output is well-formed (parse the generated HTML, validate the PDF opens) — a write-only report generator can emit broken markup that renders blank.

The report must reflect the analyzer's metrics verbatim — recomputing any metric in the report layer creates a divergence; consume the analyzer JSON as the single source and template over it, write the report file atomically.

pass1.buildNote: Safety hook must abort the run when failure rate crosses a threshold — fail loud and stop, never let a cascade run to completion silently.

pass2.systemImpact: CADRegressionSafetyHooks abort a CAD regression run on cascading failure — they protect the host (a 20K-file run that's failing every file wastes hours and memory) and prevent a corrupt run from feeding CADRegressionResultsAnalyzerEngine (U-CINF10) a meaningless aggregate. The abort must be loud and idempotent — once tripped it stays tripped for the run; a flapping breaker (trip, recover, trip) on a borderline failure rate produces a half-finished run that's worse than either a clean abort or a clean completion.

Deterministic 100-file validation means the same 100 files in the same order produce byte-identical aggregate output — the test fails loud on any extraction regression, and reverting any U-CINF fix must flip it red, or it is not a real oracle.

pass1.buildNote: Extract Mastercam Basics into structured KnowledgeTip records — route through the knowledge-conversion lanes, advisory + human-verify.

CAD-TRAINING-EXTRACT-MS0::U-CTE10.title: Consolidate hyperMILL Extractions into Action Sequences

CAD-TRAINING-EXTRACT-MS0::U-CTE12.title: Wire Action Sequences to CAD Learning Engines

csKnowledge: set-difference of seen vs known extensions
pass1.buildNote: Unknown-extension detector must surface every unrecognized file loudly — silence on an unknown extension hides a coverage gap.

pass2.systemImpact: The unknown-extension detector is the coverage-gap surface for CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0 — it feeds the coverage telemetry (U-CUC16) and the exit gate (U-CUC18) by naming every unrecognized file. A detector that stays silent on an unknown extension hides exactly the gap the 95%-coverage milestone gate exists to measure.

Surfacing must be loud but not noisy — append one advisory per newly-seen unknown extension, dedup against already-surfaced ones (a stamp/seen-set), so a recurring unknown extension doesn't spam every run.

pass1.buildNote: Customer-directory watcher must debounce to hourly via a stamp file — many Stops collapsing to one sweep, not a sweep per Stop.

If the debounce fails, either it never sweeps (stale coverage) or it sweeps every Stop (host load spike across the 13-chat fleet).

Directory-change detection by mtime/stamp has the same same-second false-negative as mtime indexing — a customer directory created and a file added within the throttle window may be partially seen; the watcher should re-sweep from the last stamp boundary, not from 'now'.

CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0::U-CUC06.title: Volume-delta alert in AGENT_CHAT.md on >5% extension-volume shift

pass1.buildNote: Volume-delta alert fires only when extension-volume shift exceeds 5% vs the stored baseline — append one advisory line, don't spam.

It mirrors the fleet-memory-monitor's single-advisory-line discipline; over-alerting trains operators to ignore it.
csDepth: Delta detection vs a stored baseline needs the baseline to be updatable — after an alert fires and the operator acknowledges, the baseline should advance, or every subsequent run re-fires the same >5% alert (alert fatigue).

Appending to AGENT_CHAT must be a single advisory line with a cooldown — concurrent appenders need atomic append (an append-only .jsonl), and the >5% threshold must be hysteretic (don't flap at exactly 5%).

CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0::U-CUC07.title: P0 gap: DXF generator — pure-JS DxfWriterEngine + bridge

pass1.buildNote: Pure-JS DXF writer must emit valid group-code pairs — round-trip the output through a DXF reader to verify, not write-only.

pass2.systemImpact: DxfWriterEngine (pure-JS DXF generator) is a P0 coverage gap — it gives CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0 a no-dependency DXF export path counted toward the U-CUC18 95%-by-bridge exit gate, and the write-path integration tests (U-CUC17) verify it. Every consumer that needs DXF output (drawings, CAM interchange) depends on it emitting loadable files.
csDepth: DXF is a group-code text format — each entity is (group-code, value) pairs in the ENTITIES section; the writer must emit the exact group codes for each entity type per the AutoCAD R12/2000 spec, and a wrong code produces a file that reads as a different entity.
Round-trip verification (write then re-parse) is mandatory — a write-only DXF test that checks 'no exception thrown' proves nothing; the test must re-import and assert entity counts/geometry match.

pass1.buildNote: Mastercam native save likely requires the NET-Hook automation API per version (.mcx-6/.mcx/.mcx-8) — verify each version writes a loadable file.

pass2.systemImpact: Mastercam native save (.mcx-8/.mcx/.mcx-6) is a P0 coverage gap — it gives CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0 the ability to write Mastercam-native files for the #1 CAM app, counted toward the U-CUC18 exit gate. Without it, parts routed through the Mastercam bridge can be read but not saved back natively.
csDepth: .mcx is a proprietary binary format — native save almost certainly requires the NET-Hook automation API per Mastercam version; the engine must dispatch on version (.mcx-6/.mcx/.mcx-8) and fail loud if the required Mastercam version isn't installed.

Verify each version writes a loadable file (re-open it) — a binary-format writer that emits a structurally-wrong file is silently broken; version-specific format dispatch must be tested per version, not assumed uniform.

CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0::U-CUC09.title: P1 gap: DWG bridge (ODA File Converter or LibreDWG)

pass1.buildNote: DWG bridge shells out to ODA/LibreDWG — handle converter-missing and nonzero-exit fail-loud, never produce a silent empty output.

pass2.systemImpact: The DWG bridge (ODA File Converter or LibreDWG) is a P1 coverage gap — it gives CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0 DWG read/write via an external converter, counted toward the U-CUC18 exit gate. As a subprocess bridge it is also a reliability surface: a converter-missing or nonzero-exit case must fail loud, not produce a silent empty file.
csDepth: External-converter subprocess bridging must handle three failure modes explicitly: converter-binary-missing (ENOENT on spawn), nonzero exit code, and zero-exit-but-empty-output — each must fail loud; a converter that 'succeeds' but produces a 0-byte DWG is the silent-corruption hazard.
Subprocess invocation needs a timeout and bounded output capture — a hung ODA converter would otherwise wedge the calling pipeline; capture stderr for diagnostics since a SIGKILL leaves no message.

pass1.buildNote: Inventor .idw export drives the COM automation API — verify the exported drawing opens and contains the expected views.

pass2.systemImpact: Inventor .idw drawing export is a P2 coverage gap — it gives CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0 the ability to emit Inventor drawing documents via COM automation, counted toward the U-CUC18 exit gate and verified by U-CUC17's write-path tests.
csDepth: Inventor .idw export drives the COM automation API — it requires Inventor installed and a live COM connection; the engine must fail loud on Inventor-not-running, not return a fake success.

Verification must open the exported .idw and assert the expected views are present — a COM export call that returns without error can still produce a drawing with missing or empty view placeholders; check the actual document contents.

CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0::U-CUC11.title: P2 gap: STL via CadQuery (trivial wrapper)

pass1.buildNote: STL via CadQuery is a thin wrapper around the Python kernel — verify the wrapper passes mesh-resolution params through, not just calls export.

pass2.systemImpact: STL via CadQuery is a P2 coverage gap — a thin wrapper giving CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0 STL export through the Python CAD kernel, counted toward the U-CUC18 exit gate. STL output feeds mesh-based downstream consumers (StltoVoxelGridEngine, 3D-print/visualization paths).
csDepth: Even a 'trivial wrapper' must pass mesh-resolution parameters through — a wrapper that calls export with default tessellation silently produces a coarse mesh; the test must verify the resolution param actually changes triangle count.
The Python CAD-kernel bridge crosses a process boundary — handle Python-missing and CadQuery-import-error fail-loud; a wrapper that swallows the subprocess error returns an empty STL silently.

pass1.buildNote: Parasolid via STEP round-trip risks geometry loss — assert B-rep fidelity (face/edge counts) survives the round-trip in tests.

pass2.systemImpact: Parasolid .x_b/.x_t support is a P3 coverage gap — it gives CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0 Parasolid interchange via a STEP round-trip, counted toward the U-CUC18 exit gate. Because it round-trips through STEP, it inherits STEP's lossy-conversion risk for any consumer of Parasolid geometry.
csDepth: STEP round-trip conversion of B-rep geometry risks losing faces/edges/topology — the test must assert B-rep fidelity (face count, edge count, watertightness) survives the round-trip, not just that a file was produced.
Parasolid .x_b (binary) vs .x_t (text) are two encodings of the same kernel format — the engine must handle both; a writer that only does .x_t silently can't satisfy a .x_b request.

pass1.buildNote: IGES is a fixed-72-column record format with linked Directory and Parameter sections — parse the column layout exactly, verify on a real .igs file.

pass2.systemImpact: The IGES .igs translator is a P3 coverage gap — it gives CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0 IGES interchange, counted toward the U-CUC18 exit gate and verified by U-CUC17's write-path tests. IGES is a legacy interchange format still common in customer file archives.
csDepth: IGES is a fixed-72-column record format with five sections (Start/Global/Directory/Parameter/Terminate) — the parser must respect exact column positions and the Directory-Entry→Parameter-Data linkage; a column-offset error shifts every field and silently mis-parses.

IGES uses parameter and record delimiters declared in the Global section — the parser must read those delimiters first, not assume the defaults (comma/semicolon); a file with non-default delimiters breaks a hardcoded parser.

pass1.buildNote: NL CAD routing tests must assert real prompts route to the correct CAD bridge — verify intent classification with concrete example phrases.

A routing regression silently sends a CAD request to the wrong bridge.
csDepth: NL intent classification is a precision/recall tradeoff — the tests must include near-miss prompts (phrases close to two bridges) and assert the right one wins, not just easy unambiguous prompts; an ambiguous prompt should surface the ambiguity, not silently pick.

Keyword + similarity routing has a polysemy hazard (e.g. a token matching multiple domains) — tests must pin the disambiguation rule with concrete example phrases, the way the /lathe polysemy guard does.

CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0::U-CUC15.title: Coverage regression test — integration smoke that all 6 bridges respond via prism_ai

pass1.buildNote: Coverage regression smoke must drive all 6 bridges through prism_ai and assert each responds — a missing-from-enum action passes a mock but breaks production.

CAD-UNIVERSAL-CONTROL-MS0::U-CUC17.title: Write-path integration tests per bridge (export verification)

pass2.systemImpact: Write-path integration tests per bridge verify export correctness for DxfWriterEngine (U-CUC07), Mastercam save (U-CUC08), DWG (U-CUC09), .idw (U-CUC10), STL (U-CUC11), Parasolid (U-CUC12), IGES (U-CUC13) — they are the regression net the U-CUC18 exit gate counts. Per-bridge fixture parameterization should share one parameterized harness across all 7 export bridges so coverage is uniform — divergent ad-hoc tests per bridge leave inconsistent assertion strength and a weak bridge slips through.

csDepth: A multi-criterion gate must AND every criterion and report WHICH criterion failed — a gate that returns a single boolean with no breakdown gives the operator no actionable signal; each of the four criteria must be a real measured check, not a hardcoded pass.

LOC-based adaptation is a control loop — it must be stable (no oscillation): a poorly-damped feed response chatters; pair the gain with a rate limiter and verify against a real cutting sequence that would oscillate without damping.

pass1.buildNote: AGI master controller orchestrates sub-engines — wire it to every engine it consumes in the same commit; a stage failure must fail loud.

pass2.systemImpact: CADCAMAGIOrchestrationEngine is the master controller for the entire CADCAM-AGI-MS0 milestone — it sequences every sub-engine (U-AGI01, U-AGI04..U-AGI19) and is wired by cadCamAgiDispatcher (U-AGI20). If a sub-engine isn't wired in the same commit it becomes an orphan; if a stage failure is swallowed, the whole AGI pipeline produces a wrong program from a silently-skipped stage.
csDepth: The sub-engine dependency graph must be a DAG with explicit stage ordering — a cycle means non-termination; topologically sort stages and fail loud on a cycle, since the orchestrator can't sequence a cyclic dependency.

A stage failure must propagate and abort the pipeline (fail-loud) — an orchestrator that catches a sub-engine error and continues produces a program missing that stage's contribution, which is worse than a clean abort; partial output must never be presented as complete.

pass1.buildNote: CadQuery bridge crosses a process boundary — handle Python-missing and subprocess errors fail-loud; verify against real geometry ops.

pass2.systemImpact: CadQueryBridgeEngine is the Python CAD-kernel bridge that gives CADCAM-AGI parametric/B-rep geometry operations — CadQueryActionExecutorEngine (U-DASAL02) and any AGI unit needing real geometry depend on it. As a process-boundary bridge it is a reliability surface: a swallowed Python error silently returns no geometry.
csDepth: JSON IPC across the process boundary must define a strict request/response schema and handle partial reads — a CAD-kernel subprocess can emit large geometry payloads; the bridge must frame messages (length-prefixed or delimiter) so a chunked read doesn't truncate.

Python-missing, OCCT-import-error, and subprocess-crash are three distinct failure modes — each must fail loud with a distinguishable error; a bridge that returns an empty result for all three hides the root cause.

pass1.buildNote: FreeCAD Path bridge translates PRISM CAM ops to Path Workbench calls — verify generated toolpaths against a real FreeCAD Path job.

pass2.systemImpact: FreeCADPathBridgeEngine integrates FreeCAD CAM into CADCAM-AGI — the AGI orchestrator (U-AGI03) routes CAM operations through it, and it is the runtime consumer of the FreeCAD Path knowledge extracted in U-CTE09. A mistranslated CAM op produces a wrong toolpath that the safety gate (U-AGI24) must then catch downstream.
csDepth: CAM operation translation from PRISM ops to Path Workbench calls is a mapping that must be total — an unmapped PRISM op must fail loud, not silently emit no toolpath; every op needs an explicit Path-call equivalent or a documented rejection.

Generated toolpaths must be verified against a real FreeCAD Path job — a translation that produces syntactically valid Path calls but geometrically wrong toolpaths is the silent-correctness hazard; verify the toolpath, not just that the calls executed.

pass1.buildNote: Mastercam .NET automation bridge must handle Mastercam-not-running and COM-error fail-loud — verify each automation call returns the expected effect.

pass2.systemImpact: MastercamAutomationBridgeEngine is the .NET automation bridge for the #1 CAM app within CADCAM-AGI — the AGI orchestrator (U-AGI03) drives Mastercam through it. As COM/.NET automation it must handle Mastercam-not-running and COM-error fail-loud, or the AGI pipeline silently produces nothing while reporting success.
csDepth: COM automation is process-affine and stateful — the bridge must manage the Mastercam process lifecycle (connect, keep-alive, disconnect) and detect a wedged COM connection; a stale COM reference throws RPC_E_DISCONNECTED unpredictably.

Each automation call must be verified for its real effect (the geometry/toolpath actually changed), not just a non-throwing return — a COM call can return success while the operation no-op'd; verify the effect.

pass1.buildNote: Inventor iLogic bridge drives parametric models by rule — verify parameter changes regenerate the model and report failures loud.

pass2.systemImpact: InventorILogicBridgeEngine is the parametric CAD driver for CADCAM-AGI — the AGI orchestrator (U-AGI03) and the parametric-part library use it to drive Inventor models by rule. The iLogic knowledge extracted in U-CTE06 is its knowledge backing. A rule that doesn't actually regenerate the model produces a stale part silently.
csDepth: iLogic rule-driven regeneration is order-dependent — parameter changes must trigger a full feature-tree regeneration and the bridge must verify the model actually rebuilt (not just that the parameter was set); an un-regenerated model is silently stale.

COM automation for parametric CAD must distinguish a regeneration FAILURE (constraint conflict, over-defined sketch) from success — Inventor can leave the model in an error state; the bridge must report that loud, not treat 'returned' as 'succeeded'.

pass1.buildNote: Stock auto-selection must consult real inventory and minimize waste — the selection chain falls through deterministically when stock is unavailable.

pass2.systemImpact: StockAutoSelectionChainEngine picks inventory-aware stock for CADCAM-AGI — the AGI orchestrator (U-AGI03) consumes its choice, and cycle-time/cost optimizers downstream depend on the stock dimension. A wrong stock selection cascades into wrong machining-allowance and cost estimates.
csDepth: A chain-of-responsibility selection must have a deterministic fall-through — when no stock matches, the chain must terminate in an explicit 'no stock available' result, not silently return the last-tried candidate; the order of handlers determines the selection bias.

Inventory-aware constraint satisfaction is a small optimization (minimize waste subject to fitting the part) — but it must read LIVE inventory; a selection against a stale inventory snapshot picks stock that's already consumed, a race with the ERP system.

pass1.buildNote: Tool auto-selection chain matches feature+material to real tool-library entries — dedupe against existing tool-selection engines before building.

pass2.systemImpact: ToolAutoSelectionChainEngine selects tooling for CADCAM-AGI by matching feature+material to the tool library — the AGI orchestrator (U-AGI03), the speed-feed engines, and ToolChangeMinimizationEngine (U-AGI14) all depend on its tool choices. A wrong tool selection produces wrong speeds/feeds and a wrong cycle-time estimate.
csDepth: There are already multiple tool-selection engines (toolselectionadvisor, toolselectionrecommender, inventoryawaretoolselector) — dedup is mandatory (R8/duplicationGuardEngine): this unit must be a chain that COMPOSES them, not a fourth parallel selector, or it duplicates an existing engine.

ISO 13399 tool-data lookup is a constraint-matching problem against the tool library — the match must be deterministic and surface ties (two equally-good tools) rather than silently picking; the chain order is the tie-break and must be documented.

pass1.buildNote: Rapid-move optimizer reorders moves to cut air time — every reordered rapid must still clear stock/fixture; safety beats time savings.

pass2.systemImpact: RapidMovementOptimizerEngine reorders rapid moves to cut air time within CADCAM-AGI — CycleTimeOptimizerEngine (U-AGI15) consumes its optimized motion, and the program safety gate (U-AGI24) must verify every reordered rapid still clears stock and fixture. A reorder that creates a collision path is a crash hazard, so safety beats the time saving.
csDepth: Rapid-move sequencing is a TSP/nearest-neighbor route optimization — exact TSP is NP-hard, so a heuristic (nearest-neighbor + 2-opt) is correct, but the heuristic's output is meaningless if any reordered rapid clips geometry; every candidate reordering must pass a collision check before acceptance.

Collision-safe retract planning is the hard constraint — the optimizer must treat retract-clearance as inviolable and reject any reordering that violates it; an optimizer that optimizes time first and checks safety after can present an unsafe path as 'optimal'.

csKnowledge: operation reordering to batch tool calls
pass1.buildNote: Tool-change minimization reorders ops to group same-tool work — reordering must preserve op dependencies (rough before finish).

pass2.systemImpact: ToolChangeMinimizationEngine reorders operations to batch same-tool work within CADCAM-AGI — CycleTimeOptimizerEngine (U-AGI15) consumes the reduced tool-change count. A reorder that violates op dependencies (finish before rough) produces a program that machines the part in the wrong order.
csDepth: Operation reordering to minimize tool changes is a constrained grouping problem — it must respect a partial order (rough-before-finish, drill-before-tap); the algorithm reorders only WITHIN dependency-compatible groups, so it is a topological-sort-then-group, not a free permutation.

Minimizing tool-change count is a set-cover-flavored problem, but the dominant correctness risk is the dependency constraint, not optimality — a slightly-suboptimal grouping is fine; a grouping that reverses rough/finish order is a defective program. Also dedup against the existing toolcalldeduplicator/batchoptimizer engines (R8).

pass1.buildNote: Cycle-time optimizer must compute time from real feed/rapid/accel physics — verify estimates against measured machine cycle times.

pass2.systemImpact: CycleTimeOptimizerEngine estimates and optimizes cycle time within CADCAM-AGI — it consumes RapidMovementOptimizerEngine (U-AGI13) and ToolChangeMinimizationEngine (U-AGI14) output, and its estimate feeds cost/quote estimation. A wrong cycle-time estimate propagates a wrong cost to the customer-facing quote.
csDepth: Cycle-time estimation is a summation of feed-time + rapid-time + dwell + tool-change overhead — accuracy requires modeling acceleration/deceleration (a short move never reaches programmed feed); a constant-velocity model systematically under-estimates time on parts with many short moves.

Estimates must be validated against measured machine cycle times — a model tuned only against itself drifts; the test should compare predicted vs real cycle time on a known program, not assert a hardcoded number.

pass1.buildNote: Part-complexity classifier scores from real geometric features — test that score moves monotonically with added features, not a hardcoded constant.

pass2.systemImpact: PartComplexityClassifierEngine scores part complexity within CADCAM-AGI — the AGI orchestrator (U-AGI03) and cost/scheduling estimators use the complexity score to allocate effort and estimate machining time. A mis-scored part biases cost estimates and capacity planning.
csDepth: ML complexity scoring (feature vector → score) must be monotonic in the obvious direction — adding a feature/pocket/hole must not decrease the score; the test should assert monotonicity rather than a hardcoded constant, which would pass even if the model returned a fixed value.

Feature engineering from part geometry is the load-bearing part — the feature vector (hole count, surface area, min-radius, tolerance band count) determines the model's ceiling; a regression/gradient-boosted model on weak features can't recover from a poor feature set.

pass1.buildNote: Master post-processor enhancement tunes per-controller output — verify generated G-code parses for each target controller dialect.

pass2.systemImpact: MasterPostProcessorEnhancement tunes per-controller G/M-code output within CADCAM-AGI — every program the AGI pipeline emits is post-processed through it for the target machine controller. Wrongly-tuned post output is G-code a real controller rejects or, worse, misinterprets, so generated G-code must parse for every target dialect.
csDepth: Controller-dialect optimization is keyed off the post-processor capability matrix — the enhancement must read the matrix per controller, not assume a generic dialect; a Fanuc-tuned output sent to an Okuma controller is the documented S[Vnn]-vs-S\d regex-trap class of bug.

Generated G-code must be parse-verified per target controller dialect — a post that emits syntactically-plausible-but-wrong code is silently dangerous; the test must run the output through each controller's parser.

pass1.buildNote: Variability integration layer must adapt to ever-changing conditions — verify it re-tunes from real outcome feedback, not a static config.

pass2.systemImpact: VariabilityIntegrationLayer adapts CADCAM-AGI to ever-changing conditions — it re-tunes parameters and strategy from outcome feedback, so the AGI orchestrator (U-AGI03) and StrategyEvolutionEngine depend on it for closed-loop improvement. If it adapts on noise or never adapts, the AGI pipeline either drifts or stagnates.
csDepth: Online adaptation must distinguish a real condition shift from outcome noise — re-tuning on every single outcome chases noise; use a drift-detection gate (conformal/CUSUM-style) so re-tuning fires only on a statistically significant shift, the same discipline as the conformal drift gate.

Feedback-driven re-tuning paired with continual learning (U-ML-11) risks catastrophic forgetting — adapting to new conditions must not erase competence on prior conditions; the layer should bound how far a re-tune can move from the prior config.

pass1.buildNote: Software router picks the CAD/CAM software by capability match — surface ties/conflicts, don't silently pick when two are equally capable.

pass2.systemImpact: SoftwareRouterEngine picks the CAD/CAM software for a job within CADCAM-AGI — the AGI orchestrator (U-AGI03) uses its choice to route work to the right bridge engine (Mastercam/FreeCAD/Inventor/SolidCAM/hyperMILL). A wrong routing decision sends a job to a bridge that can't do it.
csDepth: Capability-match routing must surface ties — when two software packages are equally capable for a feature, the router must return the conflict (R7), not silently pick; a silent pick hides a real decision the operator should make.

The feature-to-software capability lookup is a matrix that must be the single source of truth shared with the AGI bridges — if the router's capability map drifts from what a bridge actually supports, routing succeeds but the bridge fails.

csKnowledge: dispatcher action enum + Zod input schema
pass1.buildNote: cadCamAgiDispatcher: every action must be in the z.enum() AND have an executor body — a mock bypasses the enum gate, so add a real round-trip E2E test.

pass2.systemImpact: cadCamAgiDispatcher is the MCP execution surface for the entire CADCAM-AGI-MS0 milestone — it is how every U-AGI engine becomes externally callable. If an action is in the executor but missing from the z.enum(), the action is unreachable in production while a mock-based test passes; this dispatcher is the wiring that makes the whole milestone usable.
csDepth: Every action must be in BOTH the z.enum(ACTIONS) AND have an executor body — the documented RGS-TOOL bug is that MockMCPServer bypasses the SDK enum gate, so a missing-from-enum action 9/9-passes in tests while production is 100% broken; the round-trip E2E must drive the real enum gate.

The dispatcher action enum + Zod input schema is a contract — a schema change without an N-1 migration breaks every caller; validate input at the boundary and fail loud on a schema mismatch rather than passing a malformed payload to the executor.

pass1.buildNote: Full-pipeline integration test must drive CAD→CAM→post through real engines — hermetic fakes do not prove production wiring.

pass2.systemImpact: The CADCAM-AGI full-pipeline integration test is the end-to-end oracle for the whole milestone — it drives CAD→CAM→post through the real engines (U-AGI01..U-AGI20) and is the regression net the milestone close-out depends on. If it runs against hermetic fakes, the milestone ships with the integration unverified.
csDepth: Multi-stage E2E assertion must verify each stage's output is consumed correctly by the next — a test that only checks the final output can pass even if a middle stage no-op'd and a later stage compensated; assert intermediate contracts.

Hermetic fakes do not prove production wiring — the documented lesson (RGS-TOOL MS1: 97 hermetic tests missed 10 P0 bugs in the real reader factories) — the integration test must drive at least the real dispatcher and real engine APIs as the regression oracle.

pass1.buildNote: /agi-program skill must carry valid command frontmatter and route to cadCamAgiDispatcher — validate against the command-frontmatter schema.

pass2.systemImpact: The /agi-program skill is the operator-facing entry to the CADCAM-AGI pipeline — it routes to cadCamAgiDispatcher (U-AGI20). Invalid command frontmatter means the skill fails the command-frontmatter schema and may not load/trigger correctly, leaving the whole AGI milestone without a usable invocation surface.
csDepth: The skill frontmatter must validate against .claude/schemas/command-frontmatter.schema.json — a frontmatter field error makes the skill silently mis-trigger or not load; validate it explicitly, don't assume.

Skill-to-dispatcher invocation must reference the actual cadCamAgiDispatcher action names — a skill that names a non-existent action looks fine in the .md but fails at runtime; cross-check against the U-AGI20 enum.

pass1.buildNote: AGI system guide is documentation — keep CLAUDE.md a concise pointer, put detail in the wiki, reflect across all four doc surfaces.

pass2.systemImpact: The AGI System Guide is the documentation surface for the whole CADCAM-AGI-MS0 milestone — it is the operator/developer reference for U-AGI01..U-AGI24 and the doc surface the doc-reflection rule requires updating whenever any AGI unit changes. A stale guide misleads future work on the AGI system.
csDepth: Documentation-as-code: the guide must be a concise CLAUDE.md-pointer-style index into wiki detail pages, not a monolith — past ~200 lines, dense docs stop being read and CLAUDE.md compliance collapses.

The four-surface doc-reflection rule means CLAUDE.md + MEMORY.md + wiki + Obsidian memory must all be updated in the same session — an AGI guide that updates only the wiki leaves the pointer index stale.

pass1.buildNote: AGI safety gate is a hard block — it must refuse unsafe AGI output loud and unconditionally; safety constants come from physics/constants.ts.

pass2.systemImpact: The AGI Safety Gate is the hard block on unsafe CADCAM-AGI output — every program the AGI orchestrator (U-AGI03) emits passes through it before reaching a machine. It is the last line of defense against the rapid-move/feed/post regressions in U-AGI13/U-AGI01/U-AGI17; if it weakens from block to warn, an unsafe program can reach the shop floor.
csDepth: A hard-gate must be block, not warn — it refuses unsafe output unconditionally and loud; the safety-tier discipline forbids softening a block to a warn, and the gate must be on the un-disableable allowlist so a profile can't turn it off.

Safety-envelope constraint checks must use canonical constants from physics/constants.ts — inlining a safety threshold creates a drift hazard where the gate checks against a different limit than the rest of the system; the envelope (max feed, max RPM, collision clearance) is safety-critical and single-sourced.

pass1.buildNote: CadQuery action executor synthesizes a DSL method chain — verify the generated chain executes and produces the intended geometry, not just compiles.

pass2.systemImpact: CadQueryActionExecutorEngine synthesizes a CadQuery DSL method chain from PRISM actions — it is the execution arm of the DAGI action layer, consuming CadQueryBridgeEngine (CADCAM-AGI U-AGI04) to actually run the synthesized chain. A chain that compiles but produces wrong geometry silently corrupts the part the DAGI pipeline builds.
csDepth: DSL chain synthesis (fluent builder) is a sequence-to-code translation — the generated chain must be verified to EXECUTE and produce the intended geometry, not merely parse; a syntactically valid CadQuery chain can build the wrong solid.

AST/sequence-to-DSL translation has an ordering hazard — CadQuery operations are order-dependent (a fillet after a chamfer differs from before); the synthesizer must preserve the action sequence's intended order, and an executor crossing the Python process boundary must fail loud on a kernel error.

pass1.buildNote: hyperMILL action executor maps PRISM actions to the automation API — handle hyperMILL-not-running fail-loud, verify each action's real effect.

pass2.systemImpact: HyperMillActionExecutorEngine maps PRISM DAGI actions to the hyperMILL automation API — it is the hyperMILL execution arm of the DAGI action layer, backed by the consolidated hyperMILL action-sequence knowledge (U-CTE10). A mis-mapped action silently fails to produce the intended hyperMILL operation.
csDepth: Action-to-API command mapping must be total and fail loud on an unmapped action — a hyperMILL automation interface that silently ignores an unknown action produces a program missing that operation.

hyperMILL automation is process-stateful (like Mastercam COM) — the executor must detect hyperMILL-not-running and a wedged automation session, and verify each action's real effect rather than treating a non-throwing call as success.

pass1.buildNote: Inventor action executor uses Apprentice (read-only) + iLogic (write) — keep the read/write split explicit; verify write actions regenerate the model.

pass2.systemImpact: InventorActionExecutorEngine drives Inventor via Apprentice (read) + iLogic (write) — it is the Inventor execution arm of the DAGI action layer. Mixing the read-only and write paths, or a write action that doesn't regenerate the model, silently corrupts the part the DAGI pipeline builds in Inventor.
csDepth: Inventor Apprentice is a read-only API and iLogic is the write path — the executor must keep the read/write split explicit; routing a write action to Apprentice silently no-ops, routing a read through iLogic risks an unintended model mutation.

Write actions must verify the model actually regenerated and didn't enter an error state (over-defined sketch, constraint conflict) — the same regeneration-verification hazard as InventorILogicBridgeEngine (U-AGI07); a 'returned' COM call is not a 'succeeded' regeneration.

pass1.buildNote: SolidCAM iMachining bridge encodes iMachining knowledge — import chipload/engagement constants from physics/constants.ts, never inline them.

pass2.systemImpact: SolidCAMiMachiningBridgeEngine encodes SolidCAM iMachining adaptive-chipload/engagement knowledge — the DAGI action layer and any CAM strategy unit that picks iMachining technology depend on it. Because iMachining parameters drive real cutting, inlining chipload/engagement constants instead of importing from physics/constants.ts is a safety-relevant drift hazard.
csDepth: iMachining's technology-wizard parameters (adaptive chipload, engagement angle, step) are physics-relevant — they must import from physics/constants.ts; inlining a chipload constant duplicates a safety-rail value and the bridge can silently diverge from the canonical limit (the U-WIRE-ENERGY KC11 inline-vs-canonical bug class).

The iMachining bridge encodes a knowledge mapping (feature/material → iMachining technology) — it must surface when no iMachining technology fits rather than silently emitting a default; an inappropriate technology choice produces aggressive toolpaths.
